# Results — Study 410 (Cup & Handle)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The believers' claim — **a
cup-with-handle breakout (O'Neil's "pivot") launches a sustained run** — tested with the
closest **mechanical** definition of the figure on daily OHLC: swing-pivot cup + a shallow
handle + a confirmed breakout above the left-rim resistance, across **SPY + 29 US large-caps**.
We measure the forward return after each confirmed breakout as an **excess over each name's own
base rate** (does the figure beat buy-and-hold for that name?), with a one-sample/HAC *t*, a
**same-tape label-shuffle placebo**, and a synthetic positive control. Offline & deterministic
once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

> **Chart figures are partly subjective.** The cup-with-handle is the most eye-of-the-beholder
> of the classic figures. We do **not** claim to capture every cup a human would draw — we test
> one transparent, reproducible mechanical definition and say so. A different rule set would
> find a different (overlapping) event set; the qualitative verdict is what travels.

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily **auto-adjusted** (split + dividend) OHLC — 30 long-listed US large-caps incl. SPY (public, no key) |
| As-of | **2026-05-31** (last full bar **2026-05-29**; no partial month) |
| Window | 2005-01-03 → 2026-05-29 (**21.4** years; 5,385 daily bars) |
| Fingerprint | `b660382b8af3` (sha1[:12] of the close panel) |
| Detector | swing-pivot cup (depth 12–50%, rims within 6%, U-shape) + handle (≤15% pullback) + first close clearing the rim |
| Events | **443** confirmed cup-with-handle breakouts (SPY alone: **8**) |
| Timing / costs | enter the close **1 day after** the breakout (no look-ahead); hold 5/10/20/40 days; **5 bps** one-way × 2 = 10 bps round trip |

> **Survivorship (named on the Signal axis).** The basket is 30 names *still trading* in 2026.
> A fixed surviving-names panel cannot include firms that delisted after a failed breakout, which
> tilts post-breakout forward returns mildly **up** — i.e. the bias works *for* the figure, and
> it still doesn't clear the bar. Total-return adjusted closes (we label them as such).

## The signal — forward return after a confirmed breakout, EXCESS over the base rate

The excess subtracts each name's own unconditional mean forward return, so the test is **"does
the figure beat buy-and-hold for that name?"** — not "is the market up." The **placebo p** is the
share of 5,000 draws of *random entry dates on the same tape* (same count) whose excess **beats**
the observed one — the honest control for the tape's own drift.

| horizon | n events | excess mean | raw mean | win-rate | one-sample *t* | HAC *t* | placebo *p* | net of costs |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 440 | +0.21% | +0.51% | 51% | +1.28 | +1.27 | 0.41 | +0.11% |
| 10-day | 440 | +0.52% | +1.11% | 53% | **+2.14** | **+2.24** | **0.34** | +0.42% |
| 20-day | 438 | +0.06% | +1.24% | 48% | +0.18 | +0.17 | 0.49 | −0.04% |
| 40-day | 436 | −0.78% | +1.54% | 49% | −1.68 | −1.65 | 0.63 | −0.88% |

Read it carefully — this is the whole study in one table. The **raw** forward return is positive
at every horizon (+0.5% to +1.5%), which is exactly what a believer would point at. But that's
just the **base rate**: these names drift up, so *any* entry date makes money. Once we subtract
each name's own buy-and-hold drift, the **excess** collapses to noise. The one horizon that
*looks* significant — **10-day, one-sample t = 2.14** — is the textbook trap: the **same-tape
placebo p = 0.34** means a third of random date sets beat it. The *t*-against-zero is fooled by
the tape's drift; the honest arbiter says **no edge**. By 20–40 days the excess goes flat and then
**negative**.

## Costs — they barely matter, because there's no edge to tax

A round trip is **5 bps one-way × 2 = 10 bps**. Net columns above. There is nothing to erode:
the gross excess is already inside the noise band, so costs are a footnote, not the killer. (For
the rare TA rule that *does* work, costs are usually the killer; here the signal dies one step
earlier — at the placebo.)

## Robustness — loosen or tighten the detector, same verdict

| rim tolerance / handle depth | n events | excess (10d) | one-sample *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 4% / ≤10% (strict) | 415 | +0.49% | +2.18 | 0.35 |
| **6% / ≤15% (headline)** | **440** | **+0.52%** | **+2.14** | **0.34** |
| 10% / ≤20% (loose) | 455 | +0.55% | +2.37 | 0.33 |

The naive *t* hovers near 2 across detector strictness — and the **placebo p stays ~0.34
everywhere**. The "near-significance" is a property of the *up-drifting tape*, not of the figure;
no setting of the rule pulls the placebo below the bar.

## Myth check — does it beat SPY buy-and-hold? (the README hook)

The hook asks specifically about **SPY**. The detector finds only **8** clean cup-with-handle
breakouts on the SPY tape in 21 years — far too few to certify anything:

| horizon | n | excess vs SPY hold | raw | one-sample *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 8 | +0.35% | +0.59% | +0.89 | 0.34 |
| 10-day | 8 | +0.74% | +1.21% | +1.02 | 0.26 |
| 20-day | 8 | +1.18% | +2.12% | +1.30 | 0.22 |
| 40-day | 8 | +3.53% | +5.37% | +3.72 | 0.044 |

The 40-day SPY *t* = 3.72 is a **mirage of small numbers**: 8 events, and the placebo *p* = 0.044
is borderline on a sample where any 8 dates in a 21-year bull tape look great over 40 days. With
*n* = 8 there is no certifiable edge — and on the broad 443-event basket the same 40-day horizon
is **negative**. The figure does **not** beat buy-and-hold.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful

On a deterministic panel where we **plant** clean cup-with-handle shapes and a *known*
post-breakout drift, the detector + inference behave exactly as they must:

| planted edge | planted | detected | n | excess (20d) | one-sample *t* | placebo *p* | win-rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (no edge) | 160 | 151 | 151 | +0.20% | +0.41 | 0.47 | 50% |
| **+0.20** (large planted drift) | 160 | 145 | 145 | +6.06% | **+8.31** | **0.024** | 74% |

With **no** planted drift the test sits at *t* ≈ 0 and placebo *p* ≈ 0.47 (it does not
manufacture significance, and the placebo agrees); a large planted drift lights up to *t* = 8.31
with placebo *p* = 0.024 and a 74% win-rate. The detector finds the planted figures and the
inference banks a real planted edge — so the real-tape null is a genuine null, not a blind engine.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The forward return after a confirmed cup-with-handle breakout is, in excess
  of each name's own base rate, **indistinguishable from random dates on the same tape**: the only
  near-2 *t* (10-day, *t* = 2.14) is **busted by the same-tape placebo (p = 0.34)**, and 20–40-day
  excess goes flat then negative. The positive control proves the engine *can* see a planted edge,
  so finding none on the real tape is informative. Survivorship tilts the test *for* the figure and
  it still fails. **NONE, not WEAK** — the *t* that clears 2 does so only against a drifting-tape
  null the placebo corrects.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** There is no residual edge to trade. The positive **raw** forward return
  is the market beta you were always paid for (random entry dates earn the same), costs are a
  footnote because the gross excess is already noise, and the SPY-specific version rests on **8**
  events. Nothing to deploy.
- **"Beats buy-and-hold"? — BUSTED.** The believer's evidence — "the stock goes up after the
  breakout" — is **true and irrelevant**: it goes up by exactly its base rate. Subtract buy-and-hold
  and the edge vanishes; random dates on the same names do as well or better (placebo p ≈ 0.34).
  The figure is a Rorschach test on an up-drifting tape, not a launch pad.
